characters.name: Ingrid Solheim
characters.sheet: Ingrid Solheim has plotted courses for cargo ships out of Bergen for twenty years. She speaks in short, dry sentences, checks everything twice, and keeps a brass dividers in her breast pocket. She hums sea shanties when the chart is clean and mutters distances in nautical miles when it is not.

characters.name: Rahul Menon
characters.sheet: Rahul Menon has counted cash at the same counter in Kochi for thirty years. He is courteous to a fault, taps the counter twice before he says a total, and signs off every sentence with a small bow of the head. He loves cricket scores and strong coffee.

characters.name: Beatrix Whitlow
characters.sheet: Beatrix Whitlow keeps the ledgers of a Savile Row tailor and has not made an error in them since 1991. She speaks crisply, peers over her half-moon glasses, and sharpens a pencil whenever a figure needs thinking about. She takes her tea with exactly two sugars.

characters.name: Tomas Ibarra
characters.sheet: Tomas Ibarra builds staircases in Valparaiso and measures everything three times before one cut. He talks slowly, with a pencil behind his ear, and explains things in lengths, angles and board feet. He is proud, patient and a little superstitious about Fridays.

characters.name: Wren Calloway
characters.sheet: Wren Calloway drifts between mountain villages trading verses for supper. She talks in images and half-rhymes, never wears a watch, and finds numbers rather rude. She collects feathers, forgets appointments and laughs at her own metaphors.

characters.name: Fabrizio Lombardi
characters.sheet: Fabrizio Lombardi has poled the same stretch of canal in Venice since boyhood and sings to every passenger whether they ask or not. He talks with big gestures, drops opera into ordinary sentences and believes any problem can be improved by a song.

characters.name: Odalys Pryce
characters.sheet: Odalys Pryce dances with a touring company and thinks mostly in movement. She speaks in a breathless, dreamy way, stretches her calves while she talks, and describes everything as light or heavy. She is superstitious about ribbons and never reads the small print.

characters.name: Gus Pemberton
characters.sheet: Gus Pemberton spent fifty years falling over in sawdust for children and still cannot resist a pratfall. He honks a small horn between sentences, talks in jokes and riddles, and answers serious questions with a wink.
